frozen_problem.title: Finite-index Wirthmuller duality and the compact profinite Adams boundary
frozen_problem.statement: For a profinite group $G$ (having subgroups of arbitrary index), are there Wirthm\"uller/Adams isomomorphisms in $Sp^G$?
frozen_problem.selection_basis: Rank 18, score 73.5; highest-ranked eligible outside cooldown and anti-thrashing gates. PR20 was already human-merged; current main contains all nineteen prior packets. Ranked, not provisional.

theory.target: Audit the all-subgroup detection step in the compact N-free obstruction: replace an insufficient underlying-spectrum test by H=L(N intersect U) for every closed L, retaining explicit finite-quotient and compactness hypotheses.
definitions: G profinite; N closed normal; U open normal; K=N intersect U; q:G -> G/U.
X is compact and inflated from a compact G/U-spectrum; Phi denotes absolute geometric fixed points.
The N-free premise used is Phi^H(X)=0 for every closed H with H intersect N nontrivial.
A finite G-set determines a Burnside sphere endomorphism whose H-degree is its H-fixed-point count.
assumptions: G is profinite, N is closed normal, U is open normal, and K=N intersect U is nontrivial.
X is compact in the continuous genuine category and X is inflated from a compact G/U-spectrum.
N-free is used only via the condition Phi^H(X)=0 for every closed H with H intersect N nontrivial.
Finite computations test group transport and Burnside degrees, not stable homotopy groups or infinite profinite groups.
The ordinary all-subgroup proof uses primary-source inflation compatibility and compact joint detection; no kernel or independently authored proof check is claimed.
No Wirthmuller equivalence or Adams isomorphism construction is attempted.
approaches_considered: Underlying-only detection after applying Phi at K: retired by the C2 mark/cofiber counterexample.
All-subgroup thickening H=LK plus inflation compatibility and compact joint detection.
Independent finite-action and coset enumeration to test every specified transport and degree certificate.
falsification_targets: Infer genuine vanishing from underlying vanishing.
Omit normality from the product-subgroup step.
Omit nontriviality of K or extend compact detection to arbitrary integral objects.

claims.statement: The C2 Burnside vector (-1,3) has marks (1,3); among 1425 specified vectors, 57 have unit underlying degree but a nonunit degree elsewhere. The ordinary source-dependent cofiber interpretation refutes underlying-only detection.
claims.falsification_condition: An incorrect mark, omitted coefficient vector, or invalid sphere-map/cofiber interpretation.

claims.statement: Independent algorithms agree on 2273 transport rows over 25 groups, including 1322 with nontrivial N intersect U and 381 where L must be thickened to force nontrivial intersection with N.
claims.falsification_condition: Any omitted subgroup, nonnormal N or U, wrong quotient image, intersection, product or count.

claims.statement: For compact X inflated from G/U, vanishing of Phi^H(X) whenever H meets N nontrivially forces X=0 if N intersect U is nontrivial: use H=L(N intersect U) for every closed L. This ordinary argument remains unverified by an independent author or kernel.
claims.falsification_condition: Failure of closedness, normality, the inflation identity, the specified vanishing premise, or compact joint detection.

claims.statement: Balchin-Barnes-Barthel v1 supplies compact finite-quotient setup, inflation compatibility and compact joint detection; Schwede Theorem 6.16 and its following degree discussion supply the Burnside sphere-map interpretation.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong locator, category, hypothesis, or extension beyond compact objects.
